title: 4 Colour Setting Methods That You Should Apply While Preparing Your Artwork
excerpt: 4 Colour Setting Methods That You Should Apply While Preparing Your Artwork.
body:
Colour decides how your print looks. Get these four settings right in your artwork and the printed result matches what you designed.

## Use CMYK, not RGB or Pantone
Every offset and digital press builds colour from Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Black. Design in CMYK so what you see is what prints. RGB and Pantone files get converted at prepress and the colour can shift.

## Keep colour tones at 10% or above
Screens show light shades brighter than they print. Any tint below 10% tends to print lighter than it looks on your monitor.
- For a light shade, set it a little darker than it looks on screen.

## Keep total ink under 240%
A rich area might stack all four inks. Too much ink on a sheet causes real problems on press:
- Slow drying, so sheets stick together
- Smearing and set-off onto the next sheet
- Keep the four values added together at or below 240%.

## Separate similar tones by at least 10%
When two areas use a close colour, the eye cannot tell them apart in print.
- Give any two similar tones at least a 10% difference so both stay visible.

## FAQ

### Why does my print look different from my screen?
Screens emit light (RGB) and print reflects it (CMYK). Designing in CMYK and keeping light tints at 10% or above brings the two much closer.

### What is the maximum ink coverage for printing?
Keep the total of C, M, Y and K at or below 240% to avoid drying and smearing problems.

Learn more in our guide to [solid black printing](/blog/step-by-steps-to-a-perfect-solid-black-printing-and-setting/).

title: A Complete Checklist For Spot UV Printing Jobs
excerpt: A Complete Checklist For Spot UV Printing Jobs.
body:
Use this checklist before you submit any Spot UV job. It keeps your file print-ready and avoids delays or reprints.

## Images
- Spot UV can be a text, shape, solid colour, vector or picture. If it is a picture, trace out the whole area first.
- Keep every important element inside the safe zone.
- Represent the Spot UV artwork as K=100, with no gradient or tint.
- Align the Spot UV exactly with your CMYK print file.
- Do not apply Spot UV as an outline, or on gluing and folding lines.

## Text
- Use a font size of at least 5pt (Arial).
- Keep any wording inside a logo at 5pt or larger.
- Avoid fine serif fonts in Spot UV.

## Lines
- Keep line thickness at 0.5pt or above.

## Files
- Both-side Spot UV needs two separate sets of files.
- Use the correct template and remove all guidelines before saving.
- Save as PDF, 300 dpi or more, in CMYK.
- Combine everything into one ZIP file or one PDF for submission.

## FAQ

### How do I represent Spot UV in my artwork?
Draw it as K=100 (solid black) on a transparent background, with no tint or gradient, in its exact final position.

### Do I need separate files for double-sided Spot UV?
Yes. Prepare one set of files for each side.

See how to combine finishes in [Spot UV and hot stamping together](/blog/applying-spot-uv-and-hot-stamping-together-in-your-artwork-to-elevate-your-design/).

title: Applying Spot UV And Hot Stamping Together In Your Artwork To Elevate Your Design
excerpt: Applying Spot UV And Hot Stamping Together In Your Artwork To Elevate Your Design.
body:
Spot UV adds a glossy raised sheen; hot stamping presses on metallic foil. Combine them on a business card and the design looks premium. Here is how to set the files up.

## Keep the two finishes apart
- Do not overlap or stack Spot UV and hot stamping.
- Keep a clear gap between them so they do not misregister.

## Prepare four PDF files
1. **Actual print file**: the exact final look, showing where the foil and Spot UV sit. This is your master reference.
2. **Hot stamping file**: only the foil elements, in their exact positions.
3. **Spot UV file**: only the Spot UV, drawn as K=100 on a transparent background.
4. **CMYK print file**: the full-colour artwork for colour separation.

Combine the four into one ZIP file or one PDF for submission.

## Foil colours
Choose from six Pantone foils:
- 871C Gold, 877C Silver, 185C Red, 355C Green, 072C Blue, Black C.

## FAQ

### Can Spot UV and hot stamping touch each other?
No. Keep a gap between them. Overlapping the two causes registration problems.

### How many files does a combined job need?
Four: the actual print file, the hot stamping file, the Spot UV file and the CMYK file.

Order at [business cards](/business-cards-printing).

title: Artwork Orientation And Layout Explained In 2 Minutes
excerpt: Artwork Orientation And Layout Explained In 2 Minutes.
body:
Orientation and double-sided setup decide how your card comes out of production. Get it right and the front and back line up the way you intended.

## Orientation basics
- **Landscape** is wider than it is tall; **portrait** is taller than it is wide.
- Set your artwork in the same orientation you want the finished card.

## Double-sided artwork
- Supply the front and back as they should read, both the same way up.
- Tell us whether the back flips along the long edge or the short edge, since that changes how the two sides align.
- A mismatched flip prints the back upside down relative to the front.

## Folded cards
- Fat fold and thin fold change where the crease sits, so keep key text clear of the fold line.
- Design the open (flat) size, and mark the fold position on the template.

## Bleed, trim and safe area
- Extend the background 3mm past the trim on every side.
- Keep text and logos 3mm to 5mm inside the trim so nothing is cut.

## FAQ

### What is the difference between portrait and landscape?
Portrait is taller than wide; landscape is wider than tall. Design in the orientation you want the finished piece.

### Why did the back of my card print upside down?
The back was flipped along the wrong edge. Tell us whether it flips on the long or short edge when the job is double-sided.

Start at [business cards](/business-cards-printing).

title: Business Card Size: Ultimate Guide To Choosing The Perfect Size
excerpt: A comprehensive guide to selecting the ideal business card dimensions, thickness and printing method for professional use.
body:
The right business card size fits a wallet, prints clean and feels professional. Here are the standard dimensions and how to set your file.

## Standard size
- The standard card is about **3.5 in x 2 in**, the same footprint as a credit card, so it slips into any wallet.
- Unfinished (with bleed) it measures about 3.61 in x 2.11 in, which trims off the white border cleanly.

### Standard size in Malaysia
- The Malaysian standard is **9 cm x 5.4 cm**, roughly 3.5 in x 2.1 in.

## Thickness
- **14pt** is the standard weight, similar to a flyer or brochure.
- **16pt** feels closer to a greeting card and reads as more premium.
- Either way, a solid, durable card leaves a better impression than a flimsy one.

## Setting up in Photoshop
- Canvas 3.75 in x 2.25 in with a 1/8 in bleed on each edge.
- Colour mode CMYK at 300 ppi.

## FAQ

### What is the standard business card size in Malaysia?
9 cm x 5.4 cm, about 3.5 in x 2.1 in.

### What thickness should a business card be?
14pt is standard; 16pt feels more premium. Both are fine as long as the card is solid.

Configure yours at [business cards](/business-cards-printing).

title: Creating A Round Corner Business Card For Your Startup Or Corporate
excerpt: Creating A Round Corner Business Card For Your Startup Or Corporate.
body:
Round corners give a business card a softer, modern look. Here is how to set the artwork up for round-corner die cutting in four steps.

## Step 1: Download the template
Grab the business card template in PDF, Adobe Illustrator (AI) or Photoshop (PSD). Each one marks the trim line, bleed and safe zone.

## Step 2: Choose the corners to round
- Round one, two, three or all four corners.
- In the template, deselect the square corner and select the curve for each corner you want rounded.
- For a square corner, keep the square selected.

## Step 3: Save three files
1. **Combination file**: your artwork with the round-corner dieline.
2. **CMYK print file**: the full-colour artwork.
3. **Dieline file**: the round-corner cut path on its own.

## Step 4: Check and order
- Combine the three files into one ZIP file or one PDF.
- Select **Round Corner: Yes** when you place the order.

The same steps apply whether you round one corner or all four.

## FAQ

### How many files do I need for a round-corner card?
Three: the combination file, the CMYK print file and the dieline file.

### Do I need to select anything when ordering?
Yes. Choose Round Corner: Yes in the configurator so the die cut is applied.

Start at [business cards](/business-cards-printing).

title: Four Steps To Prepare Hot Stamping Artwork Using Adobe Illustrator
excerpt: Four Steps To Prepare Hot Stamping Artwork Using Adobe Illustrator.
body:
Setting a hot stamping colour in Adobe Illustrator takes four steps. This makes sure the press uses the exact foil you want.

## Step 1: Select your image
Select the text or shape you want stamped in foil.

## Step 2: Open the Pantone library
Go to **Window > Swatch Libraries > Color Books**, then:
- Choose **Pantone Metallic Coated** for Gold or Silver foil.
- Choose **Pantone Solid Coated** for Red, Blue, Green or Black foil.

## Step 3: Show the find field
In the swatch panel menu, turn on **Show Find Field**.

## Step 4: Enter the foil code
Type your hot stamping Pantone code and select the highlighted swatch. Your foil colour is now set.

## FAQ

### Which Pantone library do I use for gold foil?
Pantone Metallic Coated. Use Pantone Solid Coated for red, blue, green and black foils.

### How do I make sure the press uses the right foil?
Apply the exact Pantone code as the swatch on your stamped element, then supply a separate hot stamping file.

Learn the full setup in [tips for hot stamping artwork](/blog/tips-and-tricks-to-prepare-a-perfect-artwork-for-hot-stamping-print/).

title: Guidelines To Reverse Hot Stamping Effect
excerpt: Guidelines To Reverse Hot Stamping Effect.
body:
Normal hot stamping foils your text and leaves the background printed. **Reverse** hot stamping foils the background and leaves your text in the printed colour. Here is how to set it up.

## Use bold sans-serif fonts
- Avoid serif fonts like Times New Roman; the fine strokes drop out.
- Use a sans-serif font such as Arial, set to bold.
- Keep fonts at 10pt or larger and lines at 1pt or thicker.

## Matte-laminated art paper and art card
- If you matte-laminate art paper or art card, keep the reverse-stamped area within **35mm (H) x 70mm (W)**.

## FAQ

### What is reverse hot stamping?
The foil covers the background and your text stays in the printed colour, the opposite of standard foil stamping.

### What font works best for reverse hot stamping?
A bold sans-serif such as Arial, at 10pt or larger. Serif fonts are too fine and break up.

Next, read the [file requirements for hot stamping](/blog/tips-and-tricks-to-prepare-a-perfect-artwork-for-hot-stamping-print/).

title: Guides On Image Resolution That Every Printer Wish You Can Know
excerpt: Guides On Image Resolution That Every Printer Wish You Can Know.
body:
Low-resolution images are the most common reason a print job gets rejected. Here is what resolution means and how to keep yours print-ready.

## What DPI means
- DPI is dots per inch, the detail packed into an image.
- Higher DPI means sharper print. Print artwork should be **300 dpi** at final size.
- A 72 dpi web image looks fine on screen but prints soft and pixelated.

## You cannot fix a low-res image
- Changing a 72 dpi file to 300 dpi in your software does not add detail. The image stays soft.
- Start with a high-resolution source instead.

## Enlarging drops quality
- Scaling an image up lowers its effective DPI, so bigger means blurrier.
- Place images at or below their native size, and source larger files when you need to print big.

## FAQ

### What resolution should print artwork be?
300 dpi at the final print size. Vector art stays sharp at any size.

### Can I increase a low-resolution image's quality?
No. Raising the DPI setting does not add detail. Use a higher-resolution original.

See how to set up files in our [final artwork guide](/blog/step-by-step-in-preparing-a-final-printing-artwork/).

title: How Can Printoka's Template Help You In Preparing Your Artwork
excerpt: How Can Printoka's Template Help You In Preparing Your Artwork.
body:
A print template shows you exactly where to place your design so nothing gets cut. Printoka gives you free templates for every standard product, in PDF, Illustrator and Photoshop.

## Three lines to know
- **Full bleed** is the artwork size, larger than the finished print. Extend your background to fill it so there are no white edges after trimming.
- **Trim line** is where we cut, and the finished size. Trimming allows about 2mm, so keep borders and frames away from it.
- **Safe zone** is the inner margin. Keep all text, logos and key images inside it.

## Extra tips
- Do not add crop marks; the template handles registration.
- Remove all guideline layers before you submit.

## FAQ

### Why do I need to fill the bleed area?
So no thin white line appears at the edge after trimming. Extend your background 3mm past the trim.

### Should I keep borders on my design?
Avoid borders near the trim line. Trimming allows about 2mm, so a thin border can look uneven.

Download templates on any product page, or start at [business cards](/business-cards-printing).

title: Image Registration Issues That You Should Be Aware Of While Applying Hot Stamping Your Prints
excerpt: Image Registration Issues That You Should Be Aware Of While Applying Hot Stamping Your Prints.
body:
Hot stamping presses foil onto your print in a separate pass, so it needs precise alignment. Keep these two rules and your foil lands clean.

## Do not outline or shadow foil elements
- A foil element with an outline or drop shadow needs pinpoint alignment across two passes.
- The safer choice is a solid foil shape with no outline or shadow.

## Do not use foil as a thin frame
- A foil frame or border around your card demands near-zero tolerance and rarely comes out clean.
- Keep foil to solid shapes, logos and text instead.

## Keep it simple
Simple, bold foil elements stamp cleanly. Fine, complicated foil work invites misregistration.

## FAQ

### Can I add a drop shadow to a foil logo?
No. Outlines and shadows need alignment the foil pass cannot guarantee. Use a solid foil shape.

### Can I foil a thin border around my card?
It is not advisable. Foil frames need too much precision and often misalign.

Read the full setup in [tips for hot stamping artwork](/blog/tips-and-tricks-to-prepare-a-perfect-artwork-for-hot-stamping-print/).

title: Sending Your Artwork File To Printoka Com
excerpt: Sending Your Artwork File To Printoka Com.
body:
How you upload your file affects the print quality and cuts confusion between you and the press. Here is how to send artwork to Printoka.

## File format
- **PDF** is preferred. It holds quality and layout best.
- **JPEG** is accepted at 600 dpi or more.
- **TIFF** is accepted at 300 dpi or more.
- Vector and text look best saved as PDF.

## File name
- Avoid punctuation, symbols and non-Latin characters (! ? ( ) @ # % and Chinese, Korean or Japanese text).
- Hyphens and underscores are fine and help you tell files apart.
- Example: Business-Card-Printoka_01.

## How to send it
- Up to 20MB: upload directly when you place the order.
- Over 20MB: send us a WeTransfer link.

## FAQ

### What file format should I send?
PDF is best. JPEG (600 dpi+) and TIFF (300 dpi+) are also accepted.

### How do I send a file larger than 20MB?
Upload it to WeTransfer and share the link with us.

Set up your file first with our [final artwork guide](/blog/step-by-step-in-preparing-a-final-printing-artwork/).

title: Setting Your File In PDF Using Adobe Indesign And Adobe Illustrator
excerpt: Setting Your File In PDF Using Adobe Indesign And Adobe Illustrator.
body:
A PDF is the safest way to submit print artwork, but an outdated PDF setting can drop graphics, shift fonts or break margins. Here is how to export cleanly from Adobe InDesign and Illustrator.

## Adobe InDesign
- Export to PDF using **Adobe Acrobat 5 (PDF 1.4) compatibility or newer**.
- Newer compatibility avoids problems on updated print software.

## Adobe Illustrator
- Save to PDF using **Adobe Acrobat 5 compatibility or newer**, the same as InDesign.

## Before you export
- Outline or embed all fonts.
- Keep the file in CMYK at 300 dpi.
- Include 3mm bleed.

## FAQ

### What PDF compatibility should I use?
Adobe Acrobat 5 (PDF 1.4) or newer. Older versions may not be supported and can cause print errors.

### Should I outline fonts before exporting?
Yes. Outlining fonts prevents them shifting or dropping if the press lacks that typeface.

Then follow our [artwork upload guide](/blog/sending-your-artwork-file-to-printoka-com/).

title: Step By Step In Preparing A Final Printing Artwork
excerpt: Step By Step In Preparing A Final Printing Artwork.
body:
Printing is precise, and colour, text, lines and image resolution all shape the result. These three steps get your artwork print-ready.

## Step 1: Start from a template
Use the free Printoka template for your product. It marks the bleed, trim and safe zone so your layout, orientation and fold lines are correct from the start.

## Step 2: Place your design
- Build your design on the template.
- Merge the background and images and export them as a TIFF at 300 dpi, then place that back as the background.

## Step 3: Save as PDF
- Outline (create curves/paths for) all fonts so they convert to shapes and cannot shift.
- Combine your images and outlined text and save as a PDF.

Your file is now ready to submit.

## FAQ

### Why should I outline my fonts?
So the press does not need your exact typeface. Outlining turns text into shapes that cannot reflow or drop out.

### What resolution should the flattened background be?
Export it as a TIFF at 300 dpi at final size.

Check the details first in our [template guide](/blog/how-can-printokas-template-help-you-in-preparing-your-artwork/).

title: Step By Steps To A Perfect Solid Black Printing And Setting
excerpt: Step By Steps To A Perfect Solid Black Printing And Setting.
body:
A big black area set to K=100 alone often prints as a flat, washed-out grey. Here is how to get a deep, solid black.

## Use a rich black mix
- K=100 on its own looks weak over a large area.
- Use **C=40, M=30, Y=30, K=100** instead. The four inks overlap into a dense, even black.

## When to use each
- **Rich black (C40 M30 Y30 K100):** large backgrounds and solid fills.
- **Plain K=100:** small text and thin lines, so they stay sharp and avoid registration shadows.

## FAQ

### Why does my black background look grey?
A single K=100 ink cannot cover a large area densely. Add C=40, M=30, Y=30 under it for a rich black.

### Should I use rich black for small text?
No. Use K=100 for small text and fine lines to keep them crisp; use rich black for large fills.

Learn more in our [colour setting guide](/blog/4-colour-setting-methods-that-you-should-apply-while-preparing-your-artwork/).

title: The Limitations Of Embossing And How To Fix It For Your Prints
excerpt: The Limitations Of Embossing And How To Fix It For Your Prints.
body:
Embossing presses a die into the paper to raise your design; debossing pushes it in. Both have limits. Keep these rules and your embossing comes out crisp.

## General
- Not on gluing areas such as book spines, box assembly or folds.
- Keep the design at least 4mm from any crease or fold line.
- Do not emboss over a Spot UV area.
- Keep all key elements inside the safe zone.

## Fonts
- Minimum 11pt (Arial), including wording inside logos. Smaller text stamps as a solid block.

## Lines
- Minimum 1pt thickness, with at least 2mm between lines.
- Do not use embossing as an outline; finishing tolerance is about +/- 0.25mm.

## Dots
- Minimum 2pt, with at least 1mm between dots.
- The same applies to punctuation such as commas, full stops and colons.

## Tolerance
- Allow about 0.25mm of registration tolerance on every embossed job.

## FAQ

### What is the smallest font I can emboss?
11pt in Arial. Below that, the letters press as a solid block.

### Can I emboss near a fold?
Keep embossing at least 4mm from any crease or fold line, and off gluing areas entirely.

See the basics in [what is embossing and debossing](/blog/what-is-embossing-and-debossing-and-how-can-you-use-them-for-your-prints/).

title: The Possible Issues That Might Occur In Spot UV Printing And How You Can Avoid It
excerpt: The Possible Issues That Might Occur In Spot UV Printing And How You Can Avoid It.
body:
Spot UV lays a clear gloss coating on chosen areas and cures it under UV light. These are the setup mistakes that ruin it, and how to avoid each one.

## Lines and fonts under 0.5pt
- Thin strokes at 0.5pt or below do not coat cleanly and misregister.
- Use 0.6pt or thicker for all Spot UV lines and fonts.

## Fonts under 4pt
- Text smaller than 4pt may not coat, or fills in as a block.
- A small, detailed logo often will not coat either. Keep it simple.

## Spot UV as an outline
- Outlining with Spot UV risks misregistration and wasted stock. Use solid shapes.

## Spot UV on the trim edge
- Coating that runs to the trim can peel after cutting. Keep it away from the trim line.

## Spot UV on hole-punch areas
- A punch through a coated area lifts the coating. Keep Spot UV off hole positions.

## Where to place it
- Avoid creasing and gluing zones. Put Spot UV on the main focal point of your design.

## FAQ

### What is the minimum line thickness for Spot UV?
0.6pt. Anything at 0.5pt or below does not coat reliably.

### Why did my Spot UV peel at the edge?
It ran to the trim line. Keep the coating clear of the trim so cutting does not lift it.

Combine finishes with our [Spot UV and hot stamping guide](/blog/applying-spot-uv-and-hot-stamping-together-in-your-artwork-to-elevate-your-design/).

title: Tips And Tricks To Prepare A Perfect Artwork For Hot Stamping Print
excerpt: Tips And Tricks To Prepare A Perfect Artwork For Hot Stamping Print.
body:
Hot stamping presses metallic foil onto your print under heat. Set the artwork up right and it looks premium. Here is everything to check.

## Keep foil inside the safe zone
- Keep foil elements inside the safe zone; anything near the trim risks being cut.
- If the foil must reach the edge, extend it into the bleed.

## Business card gaps
- **Landscape:** leave a 4mm gap from the right trim and a 5mm gap from the bottom (mirror it for the opposite side).
- **Portrait:** leave a 4mm gap from the top and a 5mm gap from the right (mirror it for the opposite side).

## Minimum sizes
- Fonts 7pt or larger. Do not bold a font at the minimum size; it fills in.
- Dots at least 1.5pt; lines at least 0.5pt.
- Keep at least 1pt between dots and between lines.

## Solid colour only
- Foil cannot render a gradient. Use solid colour fills for stamped elements.

## Align everything
- Foil needs accurate registration, so align every stamped element before you submit.

## Materials that do not stamp well
- Uneven or coated stocks: Conqueror, Fine Suwen, Linen, metallic cards, super white cardstock and gloss-laminated surfaces.
- Plastic cards cannot take the heat. Avoid foil on all of these.

## Files to submit
1. **Complete file**: CMYK artwork and foil combined.
2. **CMYK file**: the same file with the foil removed.
3. **Hot stamping file**: only the foil, aligned, with the bleed area kept but changed to white.

Use a maximum of two foil colours (gold, silver, black, red, blue, green). Combine the files into one ZIP or PDF.

## FAQ

### What is the minimum font size for hot stamping?
7pt, and do not bold it at that size or it fills in.

### Which materials should I not hot stamp?
Uneven or coated stocks (Conqueror, Suwen, Linen, metallic, super white, gloss-laminated) and plastic cards.

Set the foil colour in [Illustrator](/blog/four-steps-to-prepare-hot-stamping-artwork-using-adobe-illustrator/).

title: Tips That Graphic Designers Should Look Into About Fonts And Lines
excerpt: Tips That Graphic Designers Should Look Into About Fonts And Lines.
body:
Presses allow a hair of movement as CMYK inks overlap, so fine type and thin lines are where prints go wrong. Keep these rules for sharp, readable text.

## Use 4pt or larger
- Type below 4pt blurs when the inks shift slightly, and letters look shadowed.

## Outline fonts before you export
- The press may not have your typeface, which can reflow or drop text.
- Create outlines so every font becomes a shape that cannot change.

## If you must use small text
- Avoid white text on a colour background.
- Avoid light-coloured text on white; use a heavier weight.
- Avoid thin, fine fonts; use a wider or bolder face.
- Set small text and lines to K=100 to avoid registration shadows.
- Do not use any line at 0.25pt or below.

## FAQ

### What is the smallest safe font size for print?
4pt. Below that, ink misregistration blurs the letters.

### Why should I outline my fonts?
So the press does not need your exact typeface. Outlined fonts become shapes that cannot reflow or drop out.

See also our [image resolution guide](/blog/guides-on-image-resolution-that-every-printer-wish-you-can-know/).

title: What Do You Need To Prepare For Spot UV Printing Simple And Easy Tricks
excerpt: What Do You Need To Prepare For Spot UV Printing Simple And Easy Tricks.
body:
Spot UV lays a clear gloss coating on a chosen spot and cures it under UV light. Unlike full UV coating, it hits only the area you pick, adding contrast and texture. Here is what to prepare.

## Step 1: Prepare two files
- **Actual artwork file**: your full-colour design, used for colour separation and as the reference.
- **Spot UV file**: the coated areas drawn as K=100 on a transparent background, placed in the exact position.

## Step 2: Combine and submit
- Run a final check for errors.
- Combine both files into one ZIP file or one PDF.
- For double-sided Spot UV, repeat the two files for the second side.

## FAQ

### How do I show Spot UV in my file?
Draw the coated area as K=100 on a transparent background, aligned exactly with your artwork.

### What do I need for double-sided Spot UV?
A second pair of files, one actual artwork file and one Spot UV file for the other side.

See what can go wrong in [Spot UV issues to avoid](/blog/the-possible-issues-that-might-occur-in-spot-uv-printing-and-how-you-can-avoid-it/).

title: What Is Embossing And Debossing And How Can You Use Them For Your Prints
excerpt: What Is Embossing And Debossing And How Can You Use Them For Your Prints.
body:
Embossing raises your design out of the paper; debossing presses it in. Both add a tactile, premium feel to cards, packaging and tags. Here is how they work and how to set the artwork up.

## How it works
- A metal die is made from your design.
- A finishing machine presses the die into the stock, raising the image (emboss) or pushing it in (deboss).
- Common uses: logos, patterns and illustrations on packaging, business cards and tags.

## Design rules
- Not on gluing areas.
- Do not overlap with Spot UV.
- Keep the design at least 4mm from any crease or fold line.
- Keep everything inside the safe zone.

## Files to submit
- Represent the embossed area as **C=100**, with no tint, aligned with your print artwork.
- Prepare two PDFs: the **CMYK print file** and the **embossing file** (embossed area as C=100).
- Combine both into one ZIP file or one PDF.

## FAQ

### What is the difference between embossing and debossing?
Embossing raises the design above the surface; debossing presses it below.

### How do I mark the embossed area in my file?
Draw it as C=100 with no tint, aligned with your artwork, in a separate embossing file.

See the [limitations of embossing](/blog/the-limitations-of-embossing-and-how-to-fix-it-for-your-prints/) before you start.

title: What is Hot Stamping? Why use Hot Stamping on your Prints?
excerpt: Hot stamping transfers coloured metallic foil onto a print surface under heat — here's what it is and why it makes products stand out.
body:
Hot stamping, also called foil or gold stamping, transfers a coloured metallic foil onto your print under heat. It is one of the fastest ways to make a product look premium.

## How it works
- A metal die is carved with your design.
- Heat and pressure transfer the foil from the die onto the surface.
- Used on business cards, greeting and invitation cards, book covers, labels, stickers and packaging.
- Common foils: gold, silver, copper and other metallics.

## Why use it
- **Stands out:** on a shelf, a foiled label catches the eye before the plain ones around it.
- **Feels premium:** gold and silver read as quality, which supports a higher price.
- **Strengthens your brand:** a metallic finish makes packaging and cards feel considered.

## FAQ

### What is hot stamping?
A metallic foil transferred onto a print surface using a heated metal die. It creates a shiny, raised accent.

### What can I hot stamp?
Business cards, greeting and invitation cards, book covers, labels, stickers and packaging.

title: What Is Spot Colour Printing And How Is The Artwork To Be Prepared
excerpt: What Is Spot Colour Printing And How Is The Artwork To Be Prepared.
body:
Spot colour prints one exact ink in a single run, instead of building the colour from overlapping CMYK. It keeps a brand colour consistent every time. Here is how it works and how to submit it.

## Spot colour vs CMYK
- **Spot colour:** one mixed or pure ink, printed in a single run.
- **CMYK:** the colour is built from overlapping cyan, magenta, yellow and black.
- Brands use spot colour for consistency, like Coca-Cola red or Petronas green.

## How to submit
- Supply your **actual artwork file** and note the spot colour by Pantone code or name in a remark.
- Supply a **separation file** where each spot colour is represented by one plate:
  - 1 spot colour: represent it as **K (black)**.
  - 2 spot colours: represent them as **K and M (magenta)**.
  - 3 or more: use C, M, Y, K to stand in for each colour.

## Why the extra file
Presses process a colourful job as CMYK by default and cannot tell a spot colour apart on their own. The separation file tells prepress exactly which areas print as which ink.

## FAQ

### What is the difference between spot colour and CMYK?
Spot colour is one exact ink printed in a single run; CMYK builds colour from four overlapping inks. Spot colour holds a brand shade precisely.

### How do I indicate a spot colour in my file?
Name the Pantone code in a remark and supply a separation file with each spot colour on its own plate (K for one, K and M for two).

Learn colour setup in our [4 colour setting methods](/blog/4-colour-setting-methods-that-you-should-apply-while-preparing-your-artwork/).

title: What Sticker Material Types Should You Use
excerpt: What Sticker Material Types Should You Use.
body:
Sticker labels are an important tool for branding and marketing. Pasting the right sticker on your products could attract a wide range of customers to your product.

It’s easy to see a good quality sticker and admire its artistic beauty or how it brings packaging to life but, there’s a lot that goes into creating one. You may have a look or feel in mind, but the range of features and choices is overwhelming.

This is why understanding sticker material types and their various best-case uses are essential when you’re in the process of creating or purchasing stickers for your business.

To help you through the options available, we’ve come up with an easy guide on understanding the various sticker material types and choosing the one most suitable for your use case.

## What Are The Different Types Of Stickers?

There are different types and kinds of stickers and there is no one way of classifying them. However, you can classify stickers initially based on what the sticker is made up of. This begs the question; what are stickers made up of?

No matter what unpronounceable name you see when searching for sticker materials, your stickers are likely to be made up of one of the following raw materials:

- Paper

- Vinyl

- Polyester

- Polypropylene (PP) or Biaxially-Oriented Polypropylene (BOPP)

- Satin Acetate

Each material has its pros and cons and therefore offers tradeoffs. Only by knowing your specific use case can you decide which is better suited for you.

Multiple sticker material types can be derived from these core sticker materials and we shall look further into this below.

## Sticker Format

Although this article is about sticker materials, it’s important to note that when choosing or creating stickers, knowing what sticker format suits your use case is one of the first things you have to do.

Determining the format of stickers you want influences what material you should go with and vice versa. Pick what exact material will be best for you and get your perfect stickers in no time.

Here is a brief overview of the most commonly used sticker formats and their preferred use cases.

### Singles

Usually available in standard circle, oval, or square/rectangle shapes. This is recommended for business owners or admin staff applying the stickers by hand. Stickers may be kiss-cut or die-cut.

### Rolls

Several stickers are printed on one roll for continuous placement. Most ideal for automatic label dispensers for faster application. Stickers may be kiss-cut or die-cut.

### Sheets

Show the same or different designs on one sheet. Easy to include in purchased delivery boxes as giveaways. Recommended for customers tracking the number of stickers per sheet. These stickers are usually kiss cut.

## Sticker Materials

Now there are multiple types of paper stickers or vinyl stickers or PP stickers and when it comes to choosing sticker material types, the sticker industry talks in specifics. This is where we get into details on the exact sticker material types and their best use cases. Look through to find what sticker material is best for you.

### Mirrorkorte Glossy Stickers

Mirror-coated stickers or more popularly called Mirrorkote stickers is a cast coated on paper with a mirror-like gloss on its surface. It is achieved by coating the base paper first with fine pigments and adhesive or binder and then drying up the coated surface in a cylindrical casting drum plated with chrome.

Mirrorkorte Glossy Stickers Best Use Cases

- Food Packaging

- Company Branding

- Events

- Wedding

- Box Labeling

Cons of Mirrorkorte Glossy Stickers

Like most paper stickers, Mirrorkorte stickers are not waterproof and tearproof thus they should not be used for things like bottled water.

### Woodfree Matte Stickers

A woodfree sticker is an uncoated surface with a matte touch feeling. Wood Free paper is a rough matte white paper sticker and is the most suitable choice if your aim is to not have any shiny effect. Also, this material is easy to write on and is more receptive to handwritten or drawn designs along with craft materials, such as foils and stamps.

Woodfree Sticker paper is also known as offset sicker paper. It has very good absorption of the ink and is suitable for multiple printing; it can fit with laser printing.

Woodfree Matte Stickers Best Use Cases

- Price tag

- Office labels

- Address labels

- Description labels

- Packaging labels

- Food labels

- Barcode/QR code labels

Cons of Woodfree Matte Sticker

These stickers will not be as bright as those printed on glossy sticker paper so if you’re looking for something eye-catching, it might not be the best choice.

### PP White Stickers

Polypropylene (PP) White stickers are also referred to as Synthetic Stickers. It is known for its rich luminous effect and subtle but elegant shimmer. These stickers have a strong adhesive that provides firm adhesion with water and it is tear-resistant.

White PP label stickers can be used on items that need to be washed, chilled, or refrigerated making it the ideal sticker material for food and beverage products.

PP White Stickers Best Use Cases

- Food and Beverage packaging

- cosmetic product

- drinks, frozen products

- price tag label

- microwave containers label

- Meat / Poultry

Cons of PP White Stickers

Stickers made out of PP have a typical lifespan of 6 months to 2 years so if your application requires the label to last longer than 2 years, you might consider a polyester or vinyl material.

### OPP Transparent Stickers

If you’re looking for a minimalistic and clean look for your stickers then Oriented Polypropylene (OPP) stickers are the way to go. These stickers give a ‘no-label look and allow you to display your brand while showing off the product. Moreover, OPP transparent stickers are waterproof.

OPP Transparent Stickers Best Use Cases

- bottled water

- soft drinks in PET bottles

- canned food

- household products eg detergents, fabric softeners

Cons of OPP Transparent Stickers

If not made properly, some of the problems that might occur with this material include static electricity and breakage. Like most PP materials, its lifespan is also about 2 years maximum.

### Brown Kraft Stickers

If you would like to go for an organic or handcrafted look, Brown Krafft stickers are the best option for you. Brown kraft stickers are made out of paper and are finished with a protective varnish to give a rustic and earthy aesthetic.

Another reason why you should consider using this amazing material is that it is made from 100% recycled paper so it’s very environmentally friendly.

Brown Kraft Stickers Best Use Cases

- Candle Labels.

- Flower and Florist Stickers.

- Food Stickers.

- Cosmetic Labels and Stickers.

- Soap Stickers.

- Jar Labels.

- Personalized Stickers.

Cons of Brown Kraft Stickers

Like most paper materials, brown kraft stickers are not water-resistant and are not advisable to be used for products that need washing or refrigerating.

### Synthetic Paper Stickers

These are different from regular synthetic stickers which are usually made out of polypropylene (PP) or Polyvinyl Chloride(PVC) aka Vinyl.

Synthetic papers are specially treated plastic films designed to be used by most printing processes. Synthetic paper is manufactured employing synthetic resin derived from petroleum as the main material. Its look is close to that of paper but with the durability of plastic.

Synthetic paper is an excellent option for labels that need to withstand damp environments such as coolers and freezers.

Synthetic Paper Stickers Best Use Case

- Wine bottles

- Blood bags

- Medical tubes/vials

- Shipping containers

- Restaurant menus

- Aviation luggage tags

Cons of Synthetic Paper Stickers

The cost of Synthetic paper is slightly higher and the printing process is slightly different.

### Silver Polyester Stickers

Silver Polyester Laser Labels (SP) is the go-to sticker material for technical materials.

Its weatherproof silver polyester material has a brushed silver finish and a permanent adhesive. This polyester-based material is both durable and water-resistant, making it a good choice for a wide range of applications and various temperature ranges.

Silver Polyester Stickers Best Use Case

- Product labeling

- Warehouse management

- Inventory labeling

- High-heat applications

- Wine and beer bottle labeling

- Low-temperature applications

Cons of Siver Polyester Stickers

This material is not good for squeezable packaging because it tends to pucker at the edges and polyester stickers are generally more expensive.

### Warranty Stickers

These are friable paper labels, made of high-quality epoxy resin with special technology to protect whatever surface they are put on. Once it’s applied, it is impossible to remove these labels without some damage.

If you desire, these stickers when removed can leave a residue of the word “VOID”. These stickers are extremely tear-resistant. Warranty stickers are an excellent choice for firmly covering seals or to be put on products without the intention of being removed.

Warranty Sticker Best Use Case

- Furniture

- Refrigerators, freezers

- Electronic items

- Office equipment

- Signs

- ID Tags

Cons of Warranty Stickers

These stickers are impossible to remove without leaving residue and should only be used for labels that you don’t want your consumers to remove.

## What Kind Of Sticker Material Is Best?

A simple online search could give you multiple articles claiming different kinds of sticker paper to be the best. Sticker paper veterans. However, know that the best kind of sticker paper depends mostly on what you want to use it for.

As we have established above, the sticker paper that is best for you is mostly dependent on your use case.

However, as a rule of thumb, most people want water-resistant, durable, and eye-catching stickers. This makes vinyl stickers, Mirrorkorte, and White PP stickers the most commonly used sticker materials.

If you are looking for the most sustainable and eco-friendly option, then Brown kraft paper stickers are the best for you.

## What Type Of Sticker Is Most Durable?

When it comes to durability, the sticker material that is most commonly referred to is vinyl (PVC) stickers. These stickers are built to withstand abrasion and weathering and encapsulated by another layer of clear waterproof vinyl to make a very tough and long-lasting label.

However, vinyl is said to be the most hazardous plastic for our health and is known to have high concentrations of volatile organic compounds and phthalates which can cause cancer. Thus, they are not the safest choice for things such as food, beverages, and cosmetic packaging.

We recommend a more health-friendly substitute which is Synthetic paper stickers. Just like vinyl stickers, synthetic paper stickers are built to be highly durable and withstand dampness and mild weathering.

## Summary

Although there are so many sticker material types to take into consideration when creating/choosing the perfect sticker for your business, you can be confident that the right material for you is out there.

Are you in the cosmetic or candle-making industry? Try Brown Kraft paper stickers. Do you need stickers for medical or pharmaceutical items? Synthetic paper is the way to go. Looking for something to tag your event souvenirs? Mirrorkorte gloss stickers are the go-to for that.

We hope this article has been able to make your sticker creation process a tad bit easier.

title: How Much Does Printing Cost? Quantity Breaks Explained

Print pricing can feel like a black box. It is not. A few factors set the price, and understanding them helps you order smart.

## Why price drops as quantity rises
Every print job has setup cost, plate or file preparation, and machine make-ready. That cost is shared across the whole run. Print more and the setup is spread thinner, so your price per piece falls.

## What drives the price
- **Quantity:** the biggest lever on unit price.
- **Size:** larger pieces use more material.
- **Paper and weight:** premium and heavier stocks cost more.
- **Colour:** full colour both sides costs more than one side.
- **Finishing:** lamination, spot UV, foil and die-cutting add cost.

## How to get the best price per piece
- Order at a quantity break rather than just under it.
- Combine designs into one run where the spec matches.
- Choose the finish you need, not every finish available.
- Compare a few quantities before you commit.

Setup cost is fixed and shared across the run. More pieces spread that cost thinner, lowering the price per piece.

body:
Custom apparel turns your team, event or brand into walking signage. The print method decides the feel, durability and cost.

## The main printing methods
- **DTF (direct to film)** transfers full-colour designs onto most fabrics. Great for detailed art and small runs.
- **Silkscreen** presses ink through a mesh, one screen per colour. Best value for large runs of simple designs.
- **Sublimation** dyes the fabric itself, so the print will not peel. Works on light polyester.

Browse the range at [apparel and gifts](/products/apparel-gifts).

## Which method for your job
- **Small run, full colour:** DTF.
- **Large run, few colours:** silkscreen.
- **All-over polyester print:** sublimation.

## Design tips
- Supply vector art or 300 dpi images.
- Keep fine text above 6pt so it stays legible.
- Tell us the garment colour so we set the ink correctly.

## FAQ

### What is the most durable t-shirt print?
Sublimation lasts longest because it dyes the fabric, but it needs light polyester. DTF and silkscreen are durable on cotton with proper care.

### What is the cheapest method for bulk?
Silkscreen, once the screens are set. The more you print, the lower the price per shirt.

### Can I print full-colour photos on a shirt?
Yes, with DTF on most fabrics or sublimation on polyester.

See garments and prices at [apparel and gifts](/products/apparel-gifts).

title: Digital vs Offset Printing: Which to Choose
excerpt: Understand when digital printing beats offset and when offset wins, so you order the right one for your run.
body:
Digital and offset are the two ways most print jobs are produced. Choosing right saves you money and time.

## How they differ
- **Digital** prints straight from your file. No plates, so setup is cheap and turnaround is fast.
- **Offset** transfers ink from plates to a rubber blanket to paper. Setup costs more, but each piece is cheaper at volume.

## When digital wins
- Small runs, from a few pieces to a few hundred.
- Fast turnaround.
- Variable data, like names on each piece.

## When offset wins
- Large runs, usually 1,000 pieces and up.
- Exact spot colours and consistent large solids.
- Special stocks and finishes.

## Cost crossover
For small quantities, digital is cheaper because there are no plates. As quantity rises, offset overtakes it. Configure your product and step through the quantities to see where your price break sits.

## FAQ

### Is digital or offset better quality?
Both are excellent today. Offset holds an edge on large solid colours and exact spot colours; digital is sharp for everyday full-colour work.

### Which is faster?
Digital, because it skips plate setup.

### How do I know which one my job uses?
The configurator picks the right production method for your product and quantity, and prices it for you.

Configure any product to see live pricing for your run.

title: Paper Weight (GSM) Guide: How to Choose
excerpt: Understand what gsm means and which paper weight suits business cards, flyers, brochures and covers.
body:
Gsm means grams per square metre. It is the standard way to describe paper weight. Higher gsm feels thicker and more premium.

## Common weights and uses
- **80 to 120gsm:** everyday paper, letterheads and simple flyers.
- **128 to 150gsm:** flyers and leaflets that feel solid.
- **200 to 250gsm:** postcards, booklet covers and light cards.
- **300 to 400gsm:** business cards, premium cards and box board.

## Match weight to the job
- **Business cards:** 250gsm to 360gsm.
- **Flyers:** 128gsm to 150gsm.
- **Brochure covers:** 250gsm and up over lighter text pages.
- **Packaging:** 300gsm to 400gsm board.

## Coated or uncoated
- **Coated** stock makes images vivid and resists smudging.
- **Uncoated** is easier to write on and has a natural feel.

## FAQ

### What gsm is a normal business card?
Around 250gsm to 360gsm. Heavier weights feel more premium and hold finishes better.

### Is higher gsm always better?
Not always. Flyers work best at 128 to 150gsm; going too heavy adds cost without benefit.

### What weight for a brochure cover?
Use a heavier cover, 250gsm and up, over lighter inside pages.

title: Calendar Printing Guide: Wall, Desk and Wire-O
excerpt: Choose the right calendar format, binding and paper for corporate gifts and year-round brand exposure.
body:
A printed calendar keeps your brand on a client's desk or wall for twelve months. The format decides how it is used and how premium it feels.

## Calendar formats
- **Wall calendars** hang in offices and kitchens, giving your brand a large, daily view. See [Wall Calendars](/wall-calendar-litho-printing).
- **Desk calendars** sit by the keyboard, close to hand for notes and dates. See [Hard-Stand Desk Calendars](/desk-calendar-hard-stand-litho-printing).
- **Wire-O calendars** flip cleanly month to month and lie flat. See [Wire-O Wall Calendar](/wire-o-wall-calendar-litho-printing).

Price any format at [books and stationery](/products/books-stationery).

## Paper and binding
- Use a heavier stock, 200gsm and up, so pages feel solid and resist curling.
- Wire-O binding lets pages turn fully and sit flat on a wall.
- A stiff backing board keeps a desk calendar standing all year.

## Design tips for a calendar people keep
- Give each month its own image so the calendar stays fresh.
- Leave room in the date grid for handwritten notes.
- Put your logo and contact details on every page, not just the cover.
- Add 3mm bleed and keep key text clear of the binding edge.

## Order early for the season
Corporate calendars ship in Q4 for the new year. Lock your artwork and quantity ahead of the rush so delivery lands before December.

## FAQ

### Which calendar format is best for corporate gifts?
Desk calendars stay closest to the user all day. Wall calendars give the largest brand view. Many companies order both.

### What paper weight should a calendar use?
Use 200gsm and up for the pages so they feel substantial and resist curling. A desk calendar also needs a stiff backing board.

### When should I order calendars for next year?
Order in the fourth quarter. Artwork and print run take time, and demand peaks before December.

title: Custom Mug Printing: Corporate Gifts and Merch
excerpt: Print full-colour mugs for corporate gifts, events and merch, and get the artwork right the first time.
body:
A printed mug earns daily use on a desk at home or work. That makes it one of the highest-exposure gifts you can give.

## Where custom mugs work
- **Corporate gifts** that clients actually keep and use.
- **Event and roadshow merch** with your logo and a hashtag.
- **Retail and cafe branding** sold or given with an order.

Order at [apparel and gifts](/products/apparel-gifts), or go straight to [Custom Mugs](/mug-litho-printing).

## Getting the artwork right
- Supply vector art or a 300 dpi image so the print stays crisp.
- Wrap the design around the printable area and keep the logo clear of the handle.
- Pick colours that pop against a white mug; light tints can wash out.

## Design tips
- Keep text above 6pt so it stays legible on a curved surface.
- Leave a safe margin at the top and bottom rims.
- Tell us if you want a full wrap or a single-side print.

## FAQ

### Are printed mugs dishwasher safe?
Follow the care guidance for your chosen print. Hand washing always protects the print longest.

### Can I print a full-colour photo on a mug?
Yes. Supply a 300 dpi image and we print full colour around the printable area.

### What is the minimum order for custom mugs?
Set your quantity in the configurator to see the price and any minimum for your run.

title: Sticker vs Label: Which One Do You Need
excerpt: Understand the difference between stickers and labels, and pick the right material and format for your use.
body:
People use "sticker" and "label" for the same thing, but the right choice depends on where it sticks and how it is applied. Get it right and it stays put and looks clean.

## Sticker or label: the practical difference
- **Stickers** are usually one-off, cut to shape, and applied by hand. Think laptop art, product seals and giveaways.
- **Labels** are usually applied in volume, often from a roll, to identify or brand a product. Think jars, bottles and boxes.

Both live under [labels and stickers](/products/labels-stickers).

## Choose by how you apply them
- **By hand, small runs:** die-cut sheet stickers. See [Digital Stickers and Labels](/label-sticker-digital-printing).
- **In volume on a line:** roll labels feed a machine or dispenser. See [Roll Form Stickers](/roll-form-sticker-litho-printing).
- **On glass or a car window:** static cling or vinyl. See [Car Stickers](/car-sticker-digital-static-cling-form-printing).
- **Tough, waterproof full colour:** [UV DTF Stickers](/uv-dtf-sticker-digital-printing).

## Choose by material
- **Paper** is low cost, best for indoor labels that stay dry.
- **Vinyl** is waterproof and durable for outdoor and product use.
- **Transparent** blends into glass and clear packaging.
- **Static cling** reuses without glue on windows.

## FAQ

### Is there a real difference between a sticker and a label?
Function, not material. Stickers are usually decorative and hand-applied; labels usually identify a product and are applied in volume, often from a roll.

### Which material lasts outdoors?
Vinyl with a laminate resists water and sun. Paper is indoor-only.

### Should I order sheets or rolls?
Sheets suit small hand-applied runs. Rolls suit high volumes and labelling machines.

Compare materials and prices at [labels and stickers](/products/labels-stickers).
